newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.25 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.25 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 2.25 percent in active trade on Tuesday in a continued rally which pushed the index to this year's 13th all-time high close.

The IMKB National-100 ended at 1,228, up 27 points from Monday's previous record of 1,201. In dollar terms, it also rose to a new record of 1.08 cents from Monday's 1.05 cents and Friday's previous 1.06-cent record.
Trade volume rose to 23.07 trillion lira ($202.1 million) from 19.26 trillion ($168.7 million) on Monday.

Brokers said buying accelerated in the afternoon on positive results in the Treasury's bond auction and a delay in the constitutional court's ruling on a challenge to a law designed to enable Turk Telekom's sell-off.
The Treasury sold 200.3 trillion lira nominal-valued 399-day bonds at 99.24 percent yield, down sharply from 112.42 percent in the previous 399-day bond auction on January 7.

The constitutional court began debating a call for the cancellation of the law designed to enable Telekom's sell-off. Court chairman Yekta Gungor Ozden said he did not expect a ruling to come out today.

"Activity increased in the second session under the leadership of largely state-owned shares," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank. "The market shed its cautious morning attitude after hearing that the constitutional court would not rule immediately on Telekom."
